workflow: Manually reconciling Stripe subscription payments with internal accounting records, often using spreadsheets to track chargebacks, refunds, and failed payments across multiple Stripe accounts or connected platforms.
trigger: End of billing cycle or monthly close
current_workaround: Exporting Stripe transaction CSVs, manually matching against internal logs in Google Sheets or Excel, and writing formulas to flag discrepancies.
consequence: Missed revenue from uncaught failed payments, double-counting refunds, and hours of tedious manual work that could be spent on product development.

workflow: Manually syncing customer data between Stripe, a CRM (like HubSpot or Pipedrive), and an email marketing tool (like ConvertKit or Mailchimp) — copying and pasting customer lists, subscription statuses, and contact details.
trigger: New customer signup, subscription change, or churn event
current_workaround: Using Zapier or Make with fragile webhooks, or manually exporting/importing CSV files between systems each time a customer changes status.
consequence: Broken automations lead to sending wrong emails to customers, missed follow-ups with churned users, and hours of debugging integration failures.

workflow: Manually generating and sending invoices to customers, tracking payment status, and following up on overdue invoices — often using a combination of Stripe invoices, Google Docs, and manual email reminders.
trigger: End of billing period or custom invoice request
current_workaround: Creating invoices manually in Stripe or a Google Doc, downloading as PDF, emailing to customer, then checking Stripe dashboard periodically to see if paid.
consequence: Late payments, cash flow gaps, awkward manual follow-up emails, and hours of administrative overhead that distract from building the product.

workflow: Manually monitoring server uptime, error logs, and performance metrics across multiple cloud providers (AWS, DigitalOcean, Vercel) — checking dashboards, setting up basic alerts, and manually investigating incidents.
trigger: Server error, performance degradation, or scheduled maintenance
current_workaround: Using free tiers of monitoring tools (UptimeRobot, Sentry) with limited alerts, or manually SSH-ing into servers to check logs and restart services.
consequence: Extended downtime, lost revenue from unavailable service, frustrated users, and late-night emergency debugging sessions.

workflow: Manually managing SaaS subscriptions and tool stack — tracking which tools are active, what they cost, when they renew, and whether they're still needed. Often involves a spreadsheet of all subscriptions.
current_workaround: Maintaining a personal Google Sheet with tool names, prices, renewal dates, and login credentials. Manually checking credit card statements against the sheet.
consequence: Forgotten subscriptions draining cash, paying for unused tools, security risks from orphaned accounts, and hours of administrative overhead.

workflow: Manually handling customer support tickets across multiple channels (email, Twitter, in-app chat, forum) — reading messages, triaging issues, responding, and tracking resolution status in a spreadsheet or simple kanban board.
current_workaround: Using a shared email inbox or free tier of a helpdesk (like Freshdesk free) with limited automation, or manually tracking tickets in Trello/Notion.
consequence: Slow response times, missed support requests, unhappy customers, and founder burnout from context-switching between channels.

workflow: Manually managing affiliate/referral programs — tracking referrals, calculating commissions, sending payouts, and communicating with affiliates via email and spreadsheets.
trigger: New referral or monthly payout cycle
current_workaround: Using a spreadsheet to log referral links, sales, and commission amounts. Manually calculating payouts and sending payments via PayPal or Stripe.
consequence: Inaccurate commission calculations, delayed payouts, affiliate frustration, and difficulty scaling the program without dedicated software.
